question.prompt: For Department(dept_id, name) and Employee(employee_id, dept_id, salary), explain how DDL defines keys and referential integrity and how INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE modify data. Describe a targeted salary update, the risk of a missing WHERE clause, and how foreign keys constrain deleting a department. Explain why these statements are described here rather than executed in this read-only assessment sandbox.
question.reference_answer: CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE defines structure, primary keys and a foreign key from Employee.dept_id to Department.dept_id. INSERT adds rows, UPDATE changes existing values and DELETE removes rows. A salary update uses a predicate identifying intended employees; omitting WHERE can update every row. A referenced department deletion is rejected unless its declared referential action permits it; do not assume cascading deletion. These are conceptual answers: learner sandbox execution accepts only read-only SELECT and rolls back, so it cannot run DML/DDL.
